Senses.Explanation: Lose body and life: the stated cost at points where answering, hesitating, advancing, or constructing an understanding is dangerous. The phrase occurs 645 times in 217 allowlisted texts. Xiangyan Zhixian’s tree case says that answering the question loses body and life, while silence fails the questioner. Zihu Lizong’s posted notice says his dog takes head, heart, and feet, and that deliberation immediately loses body and life. In Xuefeng Yicun’s turtle-nosed-snake case, Changqing Huileng says many in the hall will lose body and life. Baofu Congzhan says that whether one catches it or does not, one cannot avoid losing body and life. Linji Yixuan says, ‘One who acts for the teaching does not avoid losing body and life’ before recounting his three beatings under Huangbo Xiyun. Yuanwu Keqin says that whether one catches it or not, one cannot avoid the loss, then asks how this principle is. These are distinct public cases and deployment shapes of one idiom; the texts state the danger but the entry does not decide what the losses signify.
Senses.Note: The reversible form 'lose life and body' also occurs. Frequent triggers include deliberation, coming near a sword or fire, and answering a public question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若開口答即喪身失命。若不答又違他所問。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Xiangyan Zhixian section. Xiangyan is the exact hall speaker who states the tree-case double bind: opening the mouth loses body and life, while not answering violates the question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 子湖有一隻狗。上取人頭。中取人心。下取人足。擬議即喪身失命。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Zihu Lizong warns his assembly that Zihu has a dog which takes a person's head, heart, and feet and that deliberation means losing body and life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南山有一條鼈鼻蛇。汝等諸人切須好看。長慶出曰。今日堂中大有人喪身失命。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Xuefeng Yicun section. After Xuefeng raises the turtle-nosed snake warning, Changqing Huileng is the exact speaker who says that many people in the hall will lose body and life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此事如擊石火閃電光。搆得搆不得。未免喪身失命。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Mingjue (明覺禪師語錄): inside an old case raised by Xuedou Chongxian, Baofu Congzhan says that whether one catches it or not, one loses body and life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫為法者不避喪身失命我二十年在黃蘗先師處三度問佛法的的大意三度蒙佗賜杖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Linji Yixuan’s record. Linji Yixuan is the exact speaker saying that one who acts for the teaching does not avoid losing body and life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 每見入室，即云：看！看！有至劒邊擬議者，師云：嶮喪身失命了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jianzhong Jingguo Continuation of the Lamp Record (建中靖國續燈錄): in the same Shishuang Chuyuan biography, Shishuang Chuyuan arranges a sword, sandals, and water in his room and warns a hesitant entrant that he is in danger and has lost body and life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 搆得搆不得。未免喪身失命。且道。此理如何。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), Yuanwu Keqin’s hall address. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker who says that whether one catches it or does not, one cannot avoid losing body and life, then asks how this principle is.
